subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool-execution dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in tools, plugin tools, client tools, hooks, and deferred catalog tools?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose this because the feature would define a user-trusted security boundary, and the proposed process-global CLI-only shape may be incomplete for concurrent and non-CLI agent execution paths.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the request-scoped runtime contract first, then implement an additive core mode with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, hook, deferred-tool, and redaction paths.

options.title: Defer to broader safe workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until the Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode design chooses the shared vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep only command-specific dry-runs plus documented sandbox and tool-policy controls if maintainers decide global preview would be too easy to mistake for a full sandbox.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the request-scoped runtime contract first, then implement an additive core mode with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, hook, deferred-tool, and redaction paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for the shared adapter and runtime boundary where this product contract would likely be defined.
